clue.text: Seat on flight for young miscreant?

definitions.text: Seat on flight for young miscreant?

parts.words: Seat on flight for young miscreant?
parts.note: a flight here is a flight of stairs, and one stair is where a badly behaved child is sent to sit out a punishment

explanation.surface: Someone books an airline seat for a troublesome child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests an aeroplane, but it is a flight of stairs; the 'seat' is a single stair used as a time-out spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of the stair where parents send a misbehaving child to sit quietly as punishment.

clue.text: Figure lifted on horse, old knight

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the word on is read upward, i.e. backward

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A statue is raised onto a horse bearing an aged knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns ON into NO, as the clue reads upward in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry: a nine-sided polygon is a plane figure.

clue.text: International in a French running club

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the joined pair

parts.note: un is French for a
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: An international player turns out for a French running club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks part of 'running club', but it gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an association of members joined together, as a club or society.

clue.text: Sweets insect fed to drones

indicators.note: fed to means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to drone is to hum
a bug is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect is given as food to male bees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drones' looks like male bees, but it is the verb, meaning hums.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: striped boiled mint candies are a classic British sweet.

clue.text: Told what you need to get in house for dogs

indicators.note: Told signals that the phrase is spoken and the result sounds like it

parts.words: what you need to get in house
parts.note: keys to the front door are what you need to get in

explanation.surface: Someone was told the way into the dog house.
explanation.walkthrough: The words spoken as 'your keys' give the small terrier breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Yorkshire terriers, a small long-haired breed, are dogs.

clue.text: Cutlery made from soapstone undergoing deterioration

indicators.note: the letters of soapstone fall apart and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Carved stone cutlery is wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: small spoons for stirring tea are items of cutlery.

clue.text: Using force on rebellion, ousting leader

indicators.note: ousting leader means the first letter of the word for rebellion is removed

parts.note: an uprising is a rebellion

explanation.surface: A rebellion turns violent once its leader is overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Prying something open with leverage is applying force to it.

clue.text: Acknowledge fraud by company

parts.note: a con is a swindle or fraud
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Someone admits to a fraud carried out by a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to acknowledge something is to verify or affirm that it is so.

clue.text: They praise able rector's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Listeners praise a capable vicar's radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: People who celebrate are honouring or extolling something.

clue.text: Prepared pass to enter study

indicators.note: the word for pass goes into the middle of the word for study

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: A student is made ready for an exam by being allowed into a study room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' looks like an exam result or permit, but it means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having made something ready is having got it prepared.

clue.text: Sherlock's covering case of evidence gathered by doctor, follower

indicators.note: gathered by means taken inside the abbreviation for doctor
case of takes the outer letters of evidence

parts.note: a stalker is someone who follows another

explanation.surface: Clues to Sherlock Holmes's case are collected by Dr Watson, his companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives EE, the outside of 'evidence', not a detective's case.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes is pictured in a peaked cloth cap with ear flaps, his famous hat.

clue.text: What might be used to enter timber home?

definitions.text: What might be used to enter

parts.note: a log is a piece of timber
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A riddle about how one might get into a wooden house.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a door key for a log cabin; in fact it is the credentials used to access a computer system.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing term: the username and password you type to get access to a system or account.

clue.text: Cost for one picture to be replaced, acquiring new one

indicators.note: the letters of the word picture are put back in a different order, together with the two extra letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A painting is to be swapped for a new one, and someone asks what each costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be replaced' rearranges PICTURE plus N (new) and I (one), which 'acquiring' adds to the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce term: the price charged per single item or measure.

clue.text: Take back US soldier's instruments

indicators.note: back says the word for take is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to nab is to take or grab
a GI Joe is an American soldier; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A command to recover some instruments belonging to an American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take back' looks like one phrase meaning retrieve, but 'Take' is NAB and 'back' turns it into BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a stringed folk instrument with a drum-like body; an accepted plural spelling.

clue.text: Individual in Australia reported complete environmental concern

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia
one is a single individual

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: whole means complete

explanation.surface: An Australian says a whole issue is an environmental worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Individual in Australia' looks like a description of an Aussie person; 'in' merely joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinning of the ozone layer over the poles is a major ecological worry.

clue.text: Some animals pong, especially sea creatures

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that certain animals smell bad, particularly those living in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these are simple porous marine animals living fixed to the sea floor.

clue.text: Watery area in France which is beside short river

parts.note: que is French for which

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A description of a damp French region lying next to a little river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England; 'short' drops its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something aqueous consists of or resembles water.

clue.text: Irritable noble initially tried to replace king

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of the letter for king

parts.note: upright means honourable, noble
R, from rex, is king

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of tried

explanation.surface: An irritable aristocrat first attempted to replace the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone tense and easily annoyed is irritable.

clue.text: Lads keeping vanguard of Persian soldiers back

indicators.note: keeping means holding one piece inside

parts.note: sons are lads

indicators.note: vanguard of picks the front letter of Persian

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Boys holding off the advance troops of a Persian army retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to support something financially is to back it.

clue.text: Land united by saint is content for song

indicators.note: being the contents of something means sitting inside it

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A country unified by a patron saint is happy to be celebrated in song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like happy, but it means the filling of the song.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a central European country is a land.

clue.text: Crop Cockney's equally split with another adult

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the letter H

parts.note: split into equal shares is half and half

explanation.surface: A Londoner's crop is divided evenly with another grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is a London accent that drops initial H, so half half becomes ALF ALF.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: lucerne, a fodder plant, is a crop grown for animal feed.

clue.text: Cheer as drunk comes to

indicators.note: drunk says the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Cheering as the inebriated man regains consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: arriving at a place or amount is getting there, attaining it.

clue.text: Moving hen to new house, duck following

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of hen to take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so O

explanation.surface: A poultry keeper relocates a hen to a new coop, with a duck tagging along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges HEN TO into ONTHE; 'duck' is O, a score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: doing something on the hoof means doing it while on the move.

clue.text: Handle eccentric

definitions.meaning: a lever with a bent arm turned to work a machine
an odd person with strange ideas

explanation.surface: Deal with an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a bent arm turned to drive a shaft, and a person with odd obsessions.

clue.text: Stick around river to see bird

indicators.note: around means the word for stick surrounds the other letter

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: A hiker with a walking stick wanders round the river to watch birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long-legged wading bird of marshes.

clue.text: Foreign gents endorse tourism regularly

parts.note: to sign a document is to endorse it

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of tourism is taken

explanation.surface: Visiting men give their backing to tourism.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian title for men, equivalent to Mr, so they are gentlemen from abroad.

clue.text: Half ogle at that woman's tanned skin

indicators.note: Half takes just one of the two halves of the word ogle, here its second

parts.note: her is the possessive for that woman

explanation.surface: A man half-eyes a woman with a suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' gives the back half of OGLE, LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal hide that has been tanned is called leather.

clue.text: Rows about European holiday? They'll resolve who wins

indicators.note: the word for rows goes around the other pieces

parts.note: tiers are rows, as of seats
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: Arguments break out about a European holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels, but it means tiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra games or questions used to settle a contest that ends level.
